candidate: Iteration 41 CTP gateway wrapper direct-write default-deny R2 rebased on Store R5
patch_replay: Copy the Store R5 source-preimage to replay/backtrader/stores/btapistore.py, then run git -C <candidate-root>\replay -c core.autocrlf=false apply --check -p2 <candidate-root>\r2.patch followed by git -C <candidate-root>\replay -c core.autocrlf=false apply -p2 <candidate-root>\r2.patch.
test_boundary: AST-evaluated wrapper factory; fake bt_api_py.gateway.client module/client only. CTP denials assert zero provider import attempts and zero fake GatewayClient construction. No real SDK/native import, credentials/config reads, network, or broker/provider I/O.
exchange_policy: CTP exact and any CTP triple-underscore venue prefix deny; only exact BINANCE, IB_WEB, OKX, MT5 values allow direct delegation; unknown/non-string/malformed values deny. Store CTP-session classification overrides a non-CTP exchange label.
construction_policy: CTP/unknown wrapper construction creates no GatewayClient and imports no SDK; non-write operations can lazily create it through _client. Explicit supported non-CTP wrappers preserve eager client construction.
compatibility_impact: CTP Store read/connect paths retain lazy GatewayClient access, but wrapper construction no longer imports/constructs the SDK client. Non-CTP BINANCE fake construction and direct submit/create/cancel are preserved.
residuals: wrapper._client remains directly accessible; on a CTP wrapper this property lazily constructs and returns the raw GatewayClient, bypassing public wrapper guards.
Direct SDK GatewayClient construction and custom Store api/api_cls injection are unaffected.
Private guard flags/methods can be mutated or overridden by same-process Python code; this is not a hostile-code boundary.
A read/connect call on a CTP wrapper can still lazily import/construct GatewayClient and may perform provider I/O when connect is invoked; no such call was tested.
The supported non-CTP allowlist is tied to the inspected local gateway runtime registry; future exchanges require review/update.
This is not account-level authorization, production/SimNow acceptance, or writer-closure evidence.
